workflow.purpose: Keeps repeat workshop jobs suspended/resumed so specific item stocks stay inside a target band. The fortress thermostat.

algorithm_shape.controller: bang-bang hysteresis per item constraint. computeRequest(): request_resume = stock <= goalCount - goalGap; request_suspend = stock >= goalCount. Deadband between gap and goal holds last state (no chatter).
algorithm_shape.stock_counting: Every in-play item matched against each constraint: item_count/item_amount (free stock) vs item_inuse_count/item_inuse_amount (worn, in chest, assigned to stockpile, squad equipment, in a non-hauling job, inside busy container). Excludes bad flags (dump/forbid/rotten/trader/artifact...), wear>=1, thread<15000 dim, cloth<10000 dim.
algorithm_shape.arbitration: A job may feed several constraints (one per output item). Max-specificity-weight wins: resume_weight >= suspend_weight -> resume else suspend. Weight is a static specificity score of the constraint token: item subtype +10000, material category mask +100, exact material w/index +5000 / material type +1000, local/quality +10.
algorithm_shape.job_protection: ProtectedJob clones the repeat job; if the game deletes it (save/load, cancel), recover() re-creates it with exponential backoff: resume_delay starts DAY_TICKS(1200), grows 5/3 per failed recovery, capped 28 days (33600 ticks). While actually running, delay decays back toward 1200.
algorithm_shape.mapping: Lua module enumerates each job's outputs (per job_type handlers: smelting -> bars+ingots, meals -> ingredients, crafts -> ANY_CRAFT, custom reactions) and links to constraints by weakening the filter until it matches.
algorithm_shape.cadence: plugin_onupdate: light job recovery every tick; full process_constraints (map jobs, count items, flip suspends) at most every DAY_TICKS/2 = 600 ticks (half game day).
algorithm_shape.alerting: Low-stock announcement at most once per season, only when goalCount >= 3*gap and stock < min(gap*2, (goal-gap)/2). 'Cannot produce' announcement when resume requested but no job can run.
algorithm_shape.history: 28-entry ring buffer per constraint (count, amount, in_use_count, in_use_amount) persisted as int28s, powers the graph UI.

goalGap.what: resume threshold below goal; the hysteresis band

goalByCount.what: count items vs sum of stack sizes

autolabor.purpose: Assigns labors so all posted jobs get done while dwarves specialize. One plugin, three engines: legacy (write labor matrix directly), modern = labormanager (express policy through v50 work details), monitor (only watch job board for starvation).

legacy_engine.algorithm_shape: Per labor: preference order of dwarves by skill (masters of other skills deprioritized). Assign best <minimum> dwarves, then extend to dwarves who are (a) idle with no idle dwarf on this labor, (b) have nonzero skill, (c) hold exclusive labor already - until <maximum>. Exclusive tool labors (MINE/CUTWOOD/HUNT) handled specially to avoid equipment churn. Nobles penalized by responsibility: chief medical +5000, diplomats/trade +3000, manager/bookkeeper +1000. Hunting requires butchers, fishing requires fishery (building scan gate).

hauler_pct.what: percent of workforce reserved as haulers (all HAUL_* labors + clean/levers/recover wounded)

talent_pool.what: optional cap: only consider top-N most skilled

modern_engine.algorithm_shape: Every CYCLE_TICKS=61 (prime, desyncs from other cycles): (1) scan_demand counts live job postings per labor from the job board; (2) collect assignable citizens (not military/child/visitor/burrowed/limbless/in diplomacy meetings/trader requested) with top_skill + total_skill + noble_penalty + unmet-needs bias; (3) size laborer pool: laborer_target = 1 + unskilled_backlog/2 + round(n * 0.25 * starve_w), starving labors (unclaimed >= STARVE_CYCLES=5 cycles) count double; (4) rank pool by score = state_score(IDLE 0/BUSY 200/EXCLUSIVE 400/other 800) + total_skill*10 + protection(rating*40, quality-affecting skills x1.5, +usage_bonus) * skill_w * 4 + noble_penalty/100 - laborer_need_pull*4 + idle_need_pull*4 (+150 shop-permitted); lowest scores become laborers in shared work detail 'auto:Laborers'; (5) everyone else with a viable skill gets pinned to per-skill details 'auto:Skill:<name>' (pinned units protected while demand remains; tool users keep tools via detail_skill pinning); (6) guild specialists rotate rest via busy_streak; (7) apply, then labor-mapping escalation: if a posting starves despite mapped labor, enable disputed labors on idle dwarves one per cycle to A/B-identify the game's true gating labor.
modern_engine.balance_slider: 5 stops [staffing, lean-staffing, balanced, lean-skills, skills] interpolated as starve_w vs skill_w weights over the pool score

STARVE_CYCLES.what: unclaimed cycles before a labor counts double and is flagged starving

idle_reserve_pct.what: target share of workforce kept unspecialized

key_tunables.skill_usage_decay: per-cycle decay; viable skills need usage >= 0.5 to reserve details

orders.purpose: Export/import/sort/recheck the manager work-order economy as JSON - the shareable 'recipe book' of a fortress economy.

algorithm_shape.export: Serialize world->manager_orders to JSON: job/item/subtype as enum keys, material token, item_conditions (compare type + value + flag bitfields), frequency, amount_total/left, is_validated/is_active, workshop_id, max_workshops, skill-labor restrictions. Saved to dfhack-config/orders/<name>.json.
algorithm_shape.import: Additive: remaps every order id through id_mapping -> manager_order_next_id++, resolves enum keys/tokens back to raws; on unknown token the whole import fails hard (no silent partial economy).
algorithm_shape.sort: Priority: one-time orders first, then yearly, seasonal, monthly, daily. Prevents high-frequency repeat orders from starving one-time orders in the manager's daily 30-order work slot.
algorithm_shape.recheck: Flips validated orders whose conditions went stale back to Checking status so the manager re-evaluates instead of cancellation-spamming.
algorithm_shape.libraries: data/orders/: basic (food/booze/thread/pots/bags/crafts/mechanisms/soap/ash-potash/beds/paper), furnace (charcoal/glass/adamantine/melting), military (metal arms+armor with best-material checks), smelting (all ores, lower limits than military so both can coexist), rockstock/glassstock (keep small stock of all furniture types so buildingplan always has supply).

key_tunables.file_format: JSON, enum_item_key strings, condition compare types as enum keys

buildingplan.purpose: Planning mode for building placement: suspended building jobs wait until matching materials exist, then items are attached and the job finalized. Includes per-building-type default material filters (automaterial's replacement).

algorithm_shape.task_model: planned_buildings (id -> PlannedBuilding with per-filter ItemFilters + heat safety + specials) and tasks: item_vector_id -> filter_bucket -> deque of (building_id, filter_idx).
algorithm_shape.bucketing: getBucket() serializes filter pickiness into a bucket key: decorated-only Da/Db, heat H magma/fire/any, material-list size M<n> (M9 = unpicky), then full job_item + filter serialization. Buckets sort so the pickiest filters match first - a picky filter that matches nothing must not block loose filters behind it.
algorithm_shape.vector_scan_order: Scan cheap dedicated item vectors first; boulders, wood, bars, and the catch-all IN_PLAY are deliberately scanned LAST (boulders before wood before bars), so blocks are preferred for generic building material.
algorithm_shape.matching: Per bucket: on first task, filter-count available items once and cache; then for each task attach the CLOSEST matching item (distance = max(|dx|,|dy|) + |dz|) that is not in a job, passes bad-flag screen (dump/forbid/owned/in_building/construction...), not assigned to a stockpile, not in a wheelbarrow, not in ignore-burrow, and in a walkability group containing a citizen. Decrement job_item quantity; when all quantities hit 0, finalizeBuilding: sort attached items, derive building material/rough-from-boulders from first item, unsuspend (unless suspendmanager owns suspension), remove from plan.
algorithm_shape.cadence: CYCLE_TICKS = 599 (twice per game day) or immediately on cycle_requested (e.g. after quickfort places many buildings).
algorithm_shape.global_settings: Which generic building-material vectors to search: blocks/boulders/logs true, bars false; reconstruct default true.
algorithm_shape.feasibility: scanAvailableItems/countAvailableItems powers the planner UI (green/red materials, queue position per pending building).

key_tunables.bucket_key: decorated + heat-safety + material-count + full filter serialization (pickiest first)

stockpiles.purpose: Import/export stockpile settings as .dfstock protobuf files - portable logistics configs (categories, item lists, material masks) with library files in data/stockpiles.

algorithm_shape.serialization: StockpileSerializer walks every stockpile category (animals, food, furniture, stone, ammo, finished goods, cloth/leather, bars, gems...) into protobuf; export takes an includedElements bitmask for partial export.
algorithm_shape.import_modes: SET (replace), ENABLE (union onto existing), DISABLE (subtract) - plus comma-separated category filters so one file can be applied to just e.g. food. Can also apply to a hauling route stop.
algorithm_shape.lua_layer: list/status/export/import commands, safe-filename checks, directory listing of dfhack-config/stockpiles + library.
